textbookText: 2. Write the electronic configuration of potassium in terms of sub-shell. Ans:- The electronic configuration of potassium in terms of sub-shell are 1𝑠2, 2𝑠22𝑝6, 3𝑠23𝑝6, 4𝑠1.
3. What is p-block elements?
Ans:- p-block elements are a group of chemical elements in which the last (valence) electron enters the outermost p-subshell.
4. In which group of modern periodic table, are the elements with valency 2 kept?
Ans:- In the modern periodic table, elements with a valency of 2 are kept in Group 2 (the Alkaline Earth Metals) and Group
16 (the Oxygen Family).
5. How many groups combine to form p-block in a periodic table?
Ans:- The p-block in the periodic table is formed by 6 groups, namely groups 13 to 18.
6. Write the name of any two metalloids.
Ans:- Two metalloids are Boron (B) and Silicon (Si).
7. What are transition elements?
Ans:- Transition elements are the chemical elements found in Groups 3 to 12 of the periodic table that possess a partially
filled d-subshell in their atomic or common ionic forms.
8. How many groups combine to form s block in a periodic table?
Ans:- The s-block of the modern periodic table is formed by the combination of two groups, which are Group 1 (Alkali
Metals) and Group 2 (Alkaline Earth Metals).
9. What are lanthanides?
Ans:- Lanthanides (also known as the Lanthanoid series) are a group of 15 metallic elements with atomic numbers ranging
from 57 (Lanthanum) to 71 (Lutetium).
10. Mention the position of lanthanide and actinide in the modern periodic table.
Ans:- In the modern periodic table, both lanthanides and actinides are located in Group 3, but they occupy different periods
and are traditionally placed in two separate rows at the bottom of the table.
11. State the law of modern periodic table.
Ans:- Modern periodic law state that “ The physical and chemical properties of elements are a periodic function of their
atomic number.”
12. In which groups of modern periodic table do alkali metals and inert gases lie?
Ans:- In the modern periodic table, alkali metals are located in Group 1, while inert gases (also known as noble gases) are
located in Group 18.
13. Write electronic configuration of calcium on the basis of sub-shell. Ans:- The electronic configuration of calcium on the basis of sub-shell is 1𝑠2, 2𝑠22𝑝6, 3𝑠23𝑝6, 4𝑠2.
14. Write the name of the groups, in which very active metals and very active non-metals are placed in modern periodic table.

Ans:- In the modern periodic table, very active metals are placed in Group 1, while very active non-metals are placed in Group17. 15. Give the name and group of an element whose electronic configuration is 1𝑠2, 2𝑠22𝑝6, 3𝑠23𝑝6, 4𝑠1. Ans:-The name and group of an element whose electronic configuration is 1𝑠2, 2𝑠22𝑝6, 3𝑠23𝑝6, 4𝑠1 are respectively
Potassium (K) and Group 1 (the Alkali Metals).
Section ‘C’
Short answer type questions.
1. What is the cause for placing calcium in IIA group of the modern periodic table?
Ans:- Calcium is placed in Group IIA (Group 2) of the modern periodic table because it has two electrons in its outermost
(valence) shell and therefore shows a valency of +2, which is the characteristic property of IIA group elements.

Ans:- The element is Copper (Cu) and it belongs to the d-block.
ii) Write atomic number and valancies of this metal.

Ans:- The element A is Magnesium (Mg) and B is Chlorine (Cl).

5. Chlorine is more reactive than nitrogen, why?
Ans:- Chlorine is more reactive than nitrogen because chlorine needs only one electron to complete its octet, whereas
